items.good: Never have I tasted such delicious soup.
items.ko: 나는 이렇게 맛있는 수프를 먹어 본 적이 없어요.
bad: Never I have tasted such delicious soup.
Never have tasted I such delicious soup.
Never I tasted have such delicious soup.

cz.st: Never ___ tasted such delicious soup.

items.rule: Never 같은 부정 부사가 문장 맨 앞에 오면 '조동사 + 주어 + 과거분사' 순서로 바뀌어요.
items.hint: 부정의 뜻을 가진 말이 문장 앞에 나왔어요.

items.good: Rarely does my brother eat breakfast before school.
items.ko: 내 동생은 학교 가기 전에 아침을 먹는 일이 거의 없어요.
bad: Rarely my brother eats breakfast before school.
Rarely does my brother eats breakfast before school.
Rarely eats my brother breakfast before school.

cz.st: Rarely ___ my brother eat breakfast before school.

items.rule: Rarely가 문두에 오면 일반동사 문장에서는 do/does/did를 주어 앞에 두고 본동사는 원형을 써요.

items.good: Seldom is the library as crowded as it was today.
items.ko: 도서관이 오늘만큼 붐비는 일은 좀처럼 없어요.
bad: Seldom the library is as crowded as it was today.
Seldom does the library is as crowded as it was today.
Seldom is as crowded the library as it was today.

cz.st: Seldom ___ the library as crowded as it was today.

items.rule: be동사 문장에서는 부정 부사가 앞에 오면 be동사와 주어의 자리만 바뀌고 do를 따로 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: Hardly had we reached the station when the train left.
items.ko: 우리가 역에 도착하자마자 기차가 떠났어요.
bad: Hardly we had reached the station when the train left.
Hardly had we reached the station that the train left.
Hardly did we reached the station when the train left.

cz.st: Hardly ___ reached the station when the train left.

items.rule: Hardly had + 주어 + 과거분사 ... when ~ 은 '...하자마자 ~했다'는 뜻이고, had와 주어의 순서가 바뀌어요.

items.good: No sooner had she opened the door than the cat ran out.
items.ko: 그녀가 문을 열자마자 고양이가 뛰쳐나갔어요.
bad: No sooner she had opened the door than the cat ran out.
No sooner had she opened the door that the cat ran out.
No sooner did she opened the door than the cat ran out.

cz.st: No sooner ___ opened the door than the cat ran out.

items.rule: No sooner had + 주어 + 과거분사 + than ~ 형태이며, 짝이 되는 접속사는 than이에요.

items.good: Scarcely had the concert begun when the lights went out.
items.ko: 콘서트가 시작되자마자 불이 나갔어요.
bad: Scarcely the concert had begun when the lights went out.
Scarcely did the concert begun when the lights went out.
Scarcely had begun the concert when the lights went out.

cz.st: Scarcely had the concert begun ___ the lights went out.

items.rule: Scarcely/Hardly had + 주어 + 과거분사 다음에는 when이 이어져요.

items.good: Only then did I understand the meaning of the poem.
items.ko: 그제야 나는 그 시의 뜻을 이해했어요.
bad: Only then I understood the meaning of the poem.
Only then I did understand the meaning of the poem.
Only then did I understood the meaning of the poem.

cz.st: Only then ___ understand the meaning of the poem.

items.rule: Only then처럼 only가 이끄는 부사 표현이 문두에 오면 의문문 어순(조동사 + 주어)이 돼요.

items.good: Only after the storm had passed did the villagers leave their homes.
items.ko: 폭풍이 지나가고 나서야 마을 사람들은 집을 떠났어요.
bad: Only after the storm had passed did the villagers left their homes.
Only after the storm had passed did left the villagers their homes.
Only after the storm had passed were the villagers leave their homes.

cz.st: Only after the storm had passed ___ the villagers leave their homes.

items.rule: Only after ... 절이 문두에 오면 주절이 도치되어 did + 주어 + 동사원형이 돼요. 도치는 주절에서 일어나요.

items.good: Only when she apologized did he forgive her.
items.ko: 그녀가 사과하고 나서야 그는 그녀를 용서했어요.
bad: Only when she apologized he did forgive her.
Only when she apologized did he forgave her.
Only when did she apologized he forgive her.

cz.st: Only when she apologized ___ forgive her.

items.rule: Only when 절 다음의 주절은 '조동사 + 주어' 순서로 도치돼요. 도치되는 쪽은 when 절이 아니라 주절이에요.

items.good: Only by working together can we solve this problem.
items.ko: 함께 노력해야만 우리는 이 문제를 풀 수 있어요.
bad: Only by working together we can solve this problem.
Only by working together can solve we this problem.
Only by working together do we can solve this problem.

cz.st: Only by working together ___ solve this problem.

items.rule: Only + 수단·방법을 나타내는 전치사구가 문두에 오면 조동사가 주어 앞으로 나와요.

items.good: Not only did he win the race, but he also broke the record.
items.ko: 그는 경주에서 이겼을 뿐만 아니라 기록도 깼어요.
bad: Not only he won the race, but he also broke the record.
Not only did he won the race, but he also broke the record.
Not only won did he the race, but he also broke the record.

cz.st: Not only ___ win the race, but he also broke the record.

items.rule: Not only가 문두에 오면 앞 절만 도치되고, 뒤의 but also 절은 보통 어순을 유지해요.

items.good: Not until midnight did the noise finally stop.
items.ko: 자정이 되어서야 소음이 마침내 멈췄어요.
bad: Not until midnight the noise did finally stop.
Not until midnight did the noise finally stopped.
Not until midnight stopped the noise finally.

cz.st: Not until midnight ___ the noise finally stop.

items.rule: Not until ~ 이 문두에 오면 주절이 '조동사 + 주어 + 동사원형' 순서가 돼요. '~하고서야 비로소'로 해석해요.

items.good: Little did the tourists know that the road was closed.
items.ko: 관광객들은 그 길이 막혀 있다는 것을 전혀 몰랐어요.
bad: Little the tourists did know that the road was closed.
Little did the tourists knew that the road was closed.
Little know did the tourists that the road was closed.

cz.st: Little ___ the tourists know that the road was closed.

items.rule: Little이 '전혀 ~않다'의 뜻으로 문두에 오면 did + 주어 + 동사원형으로 도치돼요.

items.good: Under no circumstances should you open this door.
items.ko: 어떤 경우에도 이 문을 열어서는 안 돼요.
bad: Under no circumstances you should open this door.
Under no circumstances should you to open this door.
Under no circumstances open you should this door.

cz.st: Under no circumstances ___ open this door.

items.rule: Under no circumstances 같은 부정 표현이 문두에 오면 조동사가 주어 앞으로 나가요.

items.good: At no time did the manager mention the problem.
items.ko: 그 관리자는 한 번도 그 문제를 언급하지 않았어요.
bad: At no time the manager did mention the problem.
At no time did the manager mentioned the problem.
At no time mentioned the manager the problem.

cz.st: At no time ___ the manager mention the problem.

items.rule: At no time은 '결코 ~않다'는 뜻의 부정 표현이라 문두에 오면 did + 주어 + 동사원형이 돼요.

items.good: In no way is this decision fair to the students.
items.ko: 이 결정은 결코 학생들에게 공정하지 않아요.
bad: In no way this decision is fair to the students.
In no way does this decision is fair to the students.
In no way is fair this decision to the students.

cz.st: In no way ___ this decision fair to the students.

items.rule: In no way가 문두에 오면 be동사가 주어 앞으로 나가요. be동사 앞에 do를 덧붙이지 않아요.

items.good: Nowhere in the world will you find a view like this.
items.ko: 세상 어디에서도 이런 경치는 볼 수 없을 거예요.
bad: Nowhere in the world you will find a view like this.
Nowhere in the world will find you a view like this.
Nowhere in the world do you will find a view like this.

cz.st: Nowhere in the world ___ find a view like this.

items.rule: Nowhere가 이끄는 부사구가 문두에 오면 조동사와 주어가 도치돼요.

items.good: Not a single word did he say about the accident.
items.ko: 그는 그 사고에 대해 단 한마디도 하지 않았어요.
bad: Not a single word did he said about the accident.
Not a single word did say he about the accident.
Not a single word was he say about the accident.

cz.st: Not a single word ___ say about the accident.

items.rule: 목적어가 'Not a single ~'처럼 부정의 뜻으로 문두에 와도 did + 주어 + 동사원형으로 도치돼요.

items.good: Not once has she complained about the long hours.
items.ko: 그녀는 긴 근무 시간에 대해 한 번도 불평한 적이 없어요.
bad: Not once she has complained about the long hours.
Not once has complained she about the long hours.
Not once does she complained about the long hours.

cz.st: Not once ___ complained about the long hours.

items.rule: Not once도 부정 표현이라 문두에 오면 현재완료의 has/have가 주어 앞으로 나가요.

items.good: Rarely have scientists seen such a bright comet.
items.ko: 과학자들이 그렇게 밝은 혜성을 본 적은 거의 없어요.
bad: Rarely scientists have seen such a bright comet.
Rarely have seen scientists such a bright comet.
Rarely did scientists seen such a bright comet.

cz.st: Rarely ___ scientists seen such a bright comet.

items.rule: Rarely 뒤에는 현재완료의 조동사 have가 주어 앞에 오고, 본동사는 과거분사를 써요.

items.good: Not since last winter had the river been so high.
items.ko: 지난겨울 이후로 강물이 그렇게 높았던 적은 없었어요.
bad: Not since last winter the river had been so high.
Not since last winter had been the river so high.
Not since last winter was the river been so high.

cz.st: Not since last winter ___ the river been so high.

items.rule: Not since ~ 가 문두에 오면 '조동사 + 주어' 순서가 돼요. 여기서는 과거완료 had가 주어 앞에 나와요.

items.good: She can swim, and so can her sister.
items.ko: 그녀는 수영할 수 있고, 그녀의 언니도 그래요.
bad: She can swim, and so her sister can.
She can swim, and so does her sister.
She can swim, and so can't her sister.

cz.st: She can swim, and so ___ her sister.

items.rule: '~도 그렇다'는 'so + 조동사 + 주어'로 말하고, 앞 문장의 조동사(can)를 그대로 받아요.

items.good: I don't like spicy food, and neither does my father.
items.ko: 나는 매운 음식을 좋아하지 않고, 아버지도 그래요.
bad: I don't like spicy food, and neither my father does.
I don't like spicy food, and neither doesn't my father.
I don't like spicy food, and neither my father likes.

cz.st: I don't like spicy food, and neither ___ my father.

items.rule: '~도 그렇지 않다'는 neither + 조동사 + 주어예요. neither 자체에 부정의 뜻이 있어 not을 또 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: He wasn't at the party, nor was his sister.
items.ko: 그는 파티에 없었고, 그의 누나도 없었어요.
bad: He wasn't at the party, nor his sister was.
He wasn't at the party, nor did his sister.
He wasn't at the party, nor his sister wasn't.

cz.st: He wasn't at the party, nor ___ his sister.

items.rule: nor 뒤에서도 '조동사 + 주어'로 도치돼요. 앞 문장이 be동사 문장이면 be동사를 써요.

items.good: So tired was Jin that he fell asleep at his desk.
items.ko: 진은 너무 피곤해서 책상에서 잠이 들었어요.
bad: So tired Jin was that he fell asleep at his desk.
So was Jin tired that he fell asleep at his desk.
So tired did Jin that he fell asleep at his desk.

cz.st: So tired ___ Jin that he fell asleep at his desk.

items.rule: 'so + 형용사'가 문두에 오면 be동사와 주어가 도치되고, 결과를 나타내는 that절이 이어져요.

items.good: Such was the force of the wind that several trees fell down.
items.ko: 바람의 힘이 어찌나 셌던지 나무 여러 그루가 쓰러졌어요.
bad: Such the force of the wind was that several trees fell down.
Such was the force of the wind what several trees fell down.
Such force was the wind that several trees fell down.

cz.st: Such ___ the force of the wind that several trees fell down.

items.rule: Such가 보어로 문두에 오면 be동사가 주어 앞에 오고 '그 정도로 ~해서 ...했다'는 뜻이 돼요.

items.good: So quickly did the news travel that everyone knew by noon.
items.ko: 소식이 너무 빨리 퍼져서 정오에는 모두가 알고 있었어요.
bad: So quickly the news did travel that everyone knew by noon.
So quickly did the news traveled that everyone knew by noon.
So quickly did the news travel what everyone knew by noon.

cz.st: So quickly ___ the news travel that everyone knew by noon.

items.rule: 'so + 부사'가 문두에 오면 일반동사 문장에서는 did + 주어 + 동사원형으로 도치돼요.

items.good: Had I known about the test, I would have studied harder.
items.ko: 시험에 대해 알았더라면 더 열심히 공부했을 텐데요.
bad: Had I knew about the test, I would have studied harder.
Did I known about the test, I would have studied harder.
Have I known about the test, I would have studied harder.

cz.st: ___ known about the test, I would have studied harder.

items.rule: 가정법 과거완료의 if를 생략하면 'Had + 주어 + 과거분사'로 도치돼요.

items.good: Were I in your position, I would accept the offer.
items.ko: 내가 네 입장이라면 그 제안을 받아들일 거예요.
bad: Am I in your position, I would accept the offer.
Be I in your position, I would accept the offer.
Were in your position I, I would accept the offer.

cz.st: ___ in your position, I would accept the offer.

items.rule: 가정법 과거에서 if를 생략하면 'Were + 주어'로 도치돼요. 주어가 I여도 Were를 써요.

items.good: Should you need any help, please call me.
items.ko: 혹시 도움이 필요하면 저에게 전화하세요.
bad: Should you needs any help, please call me.
Do you need any help, please call me.
Should need you any help, please call me.

cz.st: ___ need any help, please call me.

items.rule: '혹시 ~한다면'의 if절은 if를 빼고 'Should + 주어 + 동사원형'으로 쓸 수 있어요.

items.good: Had it not been for your advice, I would have failed the exam.
items.ko: 네 조언이 없었다면 나는 시험에 떨어졌을 거예요.
bad: Had not it been for your advice, I would have failed the exam.
Had it not be for your advice, I would have failed the exam.
Not had it been for your advice, I would have failed the exam.

cz.st: ___ it not been for your advice, I would have failed the exam.

items.rule: If it had not been for ~ 에서 if를 생략하면 Had it not been for ~ 가 돼요. not은 주어 뒤에 와요.

items.good: Here she comes now, right on time.
items.ko: 그녀가 오네요, 딱 맞춰서요.
bad: Here comes she now, right on time.
Here does she come now, right on time.
Here is she coming now, right on time.

cz.st: Here ___ now, right on time.

items.rule: Here/There 뒤에 오는 주어가 대명사이면 도치하지 않고 'Here she comes'로 말해요. 명사 주어일 때만 'Here comes the bus'처럼 도치해요.

items.good: On the top of the hill stands an old castle.
items.ko: 언덕 꼭대기에는 오래된 성이 서 있어요.
bad: On the top of the hill stand an old castle.
On the top of the hill does stands an old castle.
On the top of the hill is stands an old castle.

cz.st: On the top of the hill ___ an old castle.

items.rule: 장소 부사구가 문두에 오면 '동사 + 주어'로 도치될 수 있고, 동사는 뒤에 오는 진짜 주어(an old castle)에 수를 일치시켜요.

items.good: Beside the lake live two old fishermen.
items.ko: 호숫가에는 나이 많은 어부 두 명이 살고 있어요.
bad: Beside the lake lives two old fishermen.
Beside the lake does live two old fishermen.
Beside the lake they live two old fishermen.

cz.st: Beside the lake ___ two old fishermen.

items.rule: 장소 표현이 문두에 오면 동사가 주어 앞에 오고, 동사는 뒤의 주어(two old fishermen)에 맞춰 복수형을 써요.

items.good: It was Mina who broke the vase, not her brother.
items.ko: 꽃병을 깬 사람은 그녀의 오빠가 아니라 미나였어요.
bad: It was Mina which broke the vase, not her brother.
It were Mina who broke the vase, not her brother.
Was Mina who broke the vase, not her brother.

cz.st: It was Mina ___ broke the vase, not her brother.

items.rule: It is/was ~ who(that) ... 강조 구문에서 강조되는 말이 사람이면 who 또는 that을 써요. which와 what은 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: It was in the park that I first met Daniel.
items.ko: 내가 다니엘을 처음 만난 곳은 바로 공원이었어요.
bad: It was in the park what I first met Daniel.
It was in the park I that first met Daniel.
It in the park was that I first met Daniel.

cz.st: It was in the park ___ I first met Daniel.

items.rule: 장소 부사구를 강조할 때는 It is/was + 장소 + that + 나머지 문장의 순서를 써요.

items.good: It was not until I moved abroad that I appreciated my hometown.
items.ko: 외국으로 이사하고 나서야 나는 고향의 소중함을 알게 되었어요.
bad: It was not until I moved abroad what I appreciated my hometown.
It was not until did I move abroad that I appreciated my hometown.
Not until I moved abroad it was that I appreciated my hometown.

cz.st: It was not until I moved abroad ___ I appreciated my hometown.

items.rule: It is/was not until ~ that ... 은 '~하고서야 비로소 ...했다'는 뜻의 강조 구문이에요. 이때는 도치되지 않아요.

items.good: What I need most is a good night's sleep.
items.ko: 내가 가장 필요한 것은 푹 자는 거예요.
bad: What I need most are a good night's sleep.
That I need most is a good night's sleep.
What I need most it is a good night's sleep.

cz.st: ___ I need most is a good night's sleep.

items.rule: What ~ is ... 구문은 '~하는 것은 ...이다'라는 뜻으로 바로 뒤의 내용을 강조해요.

items.good: What surprised everyone was that he finished first.
items.ko: 모두를 놀라게 한 것은 그가 일등으로 들어왔다는 점이었어요.
bad: What surprised everyone were that he finished first.
What surprised everyone it was that he finished first.
That surprised everyone was that he finished first.

cz.st: What surprised everyone ___ that he finished first.

items.rule: What이 이끄는 명사절은 단수 취급하고, 시제는 문장 전체에 맞춰요.

items.good: What she did was call the police immediately.
items.ko: 그녀가 한 일은 즉시 경찰에 신고한 것이었어요.
bad: What she did was calls the police immediately.
What she did called the police immediately.
What did she was call the police immediately.

cz.st: What she did was ___ the police immediately.

items.rule: What ... did was 뒤에는 동사원형(또는 to 부정사)을 써서 한 일을 강조해요.

items.good: I do enjoy hiking, even though it is tiring.
items.ko: 힘들긴 해도 나는 등산을 정말 좋아해요.
bad: I does enjoy hiking, even though it is tiring.
I do enjoys hiking, even though it is tiring.
I am do enjoy hiking, even though it is tiring.

cz.st: I ___ enjoy hiking, even though it is tiring.

items.rule: 동사 앞에 do/does/did를 쓰면 '정말 ~하다'라는 강조가 돼요. 이때 본동사는 원형이에요.

items.good: She did try to call you, but your phone was off.
items.ko: 그녀는 너에게 정말 전화하려고 했지만 네 전화기가 꺼져 있었어요.
bad: She did tried to call you, but your phone was off.
She do try to call you, but your phone was off.
She did tries to call you, but your phone was off.

items.title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Daughter
items.text: Rarely did visitors climb the narrow stairs of Pine Point Lighthouse, but Nora did it every evening. Her father kept the light, and she liked to watch him polish the huge glass lens until it shone. Only when the sun had completely set did he switch it on. One stormy night, a fishing boat lost its way in the fog. Not until Nora noticed a tiny red lantern near the rocks did she understand that someone needed help. She shouted to her father, and together they flashed the light in a steady pattern. It was this signal that guided the boat safely into the harbor. Nora never forgot that night.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A father who teaches his daughter to sail
A lighthouse that is closed to all visitors
A girl who helps a boat reach safety
A fishing trip that ends with a big catch

After the sun had set

Right after the storm ended

o: She saw a small red lantern near the rocks.

items.title: Why Teenagers Need Sleep
items.text: Many teenagers believe they can succeed on very little sleep, but research suggests otherwise. Experts recommend that people aged thirteen to eighteen sleep between eight and ten hours each night. Not only does enough sleep improve memory, but it also helps students control their emotions. During sleep, the brain organizes what was learned during the day. That is why staying up all night to study often backfires. Seldom do students who sleep five hours perform as well on tests as those who rest properly. It is the habit of going to bed at a regular time that matters most. Small changes, such as turning off screens an hour earlier, can make a real difference.

qs.q: What is the main point of the passage?
o: Studying late at night is the best way to remember lessons.
Regular, sufficient sleep helps teenagers learn and feel better.
Screens are the only reason teenagers sleep too little.
Sleeping extra hours always makes tests much easier.
qs.why: 충분하고 규칙적인 수면이 학습과 정서에 도움이 된다는 것이 글의 요지예요.

qs.q: How many hours of sleep do experts recommend for teenagers?
o: Eight to ten
Five to seven
Six to eight
Ten to twelve
qs.why: 'between eight and ten hours each night'라고 했어요.

qs.q: Why does the writer say that staying up all night often backfires?
o: Students forget to eat during all-night study.
Late-night lights make reading much harder.
Teachers give more difficult tests the next day.
The brain needs sleep to organize what was learned.
qs.why: 잠자는 동안 뇌가 낮에 배운 것을 정리하기 때문에 밤샘 공부는 오히려 역효과가 나요.

qs.q: In the passage, "backfires" is closest in meaning to

is done with friends
produces the opposite result

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude toward going to bed at a regular time?

Positive, because it matters most
Neutral, because research is unclear

qs.why: 규칙적인 취침 습관이 가장 중요하다고 말하므로 긍정적인 태도예요.

items.title: The Harvest Lantern Festival
items.text: Every October, the town of Willow Creek holds a lantern festival to celebrate the end of the harvest. Not only do families decorate the streets with paper lanterns, but they also share dishes made from the season's crops. At sunset, children carry their own lanterns in a slow parade to the river. Only then does the mayor light the large lantern in the town square, which signals the start of the music. Many visitors say it is the quiet moment before the music that they remember best. Local artists sell handmade crafts, and the money goes to the school library. By midnight, the last lantern floats down the river.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A town's yearly lantern celebration
A mayor's plan to build a new library
A school contest for the best handmade craft
A farmers' meeting about next year's crops
qs.why: 윌로 크릭 마을의 연례 등불 축제를 소개하는 글이에요.

qs.q: Where does the money from the crafts go?

To the river park
To the mayor's office
To the school library

qs.q: When does the music start?
o: As soon as the children begin the parade
When families finish their dinner
After the mayor lights the large lantern
After the last lantern floats away
qs.why: 시장이 큰 등불을 밝히는 것이 음악 시작의 신호예요.

qs.q: In the passage, "signals" is closest in meaning to

shows that something is about to begin
makes the lanterns brighter

qs.q: What can be inferred about the visitors' favorite moment?

The loud music played in the town square
The sale of handmade crafts
The sharing of food at dinner

items.title: Octopus Intelligence
items.text: Octopuses are among the most intelligent animals in the ocean. In laboratory tests, some have learned to unscrew jar lids to reach food inside. Others have escaped from tanks that scientists thought were secure. An octopus has about five hundred million nerve cells, and most of them are in its arms rather than its head. Little did researchers expect that each arm could react to touch and taste on its own. Most kinds live only one to three years, which surprises people who admire their skills. Because the young hatch without parents nearby, they cannot learn from adults. It is through experience alone that they gain their knowledge.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?

Scientists build tanks that no animal can leave.
Jar lids are the favorite food of sea animals.
Octopuses show surprising intelligence in short lives.

qs.q: Where are most of an octopus's nerve cells?

easy to see

items.title: E-bikes in the City
items.text: In many cities, electric bicycles are changing the way people travel to work. An e-bike has a small motor that helps the rider climb hills without getting tired. Supporters point out that it costs far less to charge than to fuel a car. Never before have so many commuters had such a cheap and clean alternative. However, not everyone is pleased. Some pedestrians complain that riders move too fast on crowded sidewalks. Only when cities build more bike lanes will these conflicts decrease, according to traffic experts. Others worry about batteries, which must be recycled carefully. Overall, e-bikes offer real benefits, but they work best when roads are designed for them.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?

Why cars will disappear from every city
The advantages and problems of e-bikes
A race between riders on steep hills

When cars are banned from cities

items.title: A Shy Speaker
items.text: When Haru joined the debate club, he could hardly speak in front of ten classmates. Not until his second month did he dare to raise his hand. His coach, Ms. Park, never pushed him; instead, she gave him small tasks, such as timing the other students' speeches. It was this gentle approach that slowly built his confidence. By spring, Haru was arguing for school uniforms in front of fifty parents. Though his voice shook at first, he finished with a strong closing statement. Afterward, a parent asked how he had changed so much. He smiled and said that listening carefully to others had taught him how to speak.

items.title: Hanji, Paper with a Long Story
items.text: Hanji is the traditional paper of Korea, made from the inner bark of the mulberry tree. Unlike ordinary paper, it is produced by hand, with fibers spread evenly in water before being dried in thin sheets. Rarely does hanji tear easily, which is why it was used for books, doors, and boxes in the past. Today, artists have found new uses for it, from lamps to colorful sculptures. Little do many visitors realize that the paper also lets air pass through, so rooms covered with it stay comfortable. It is craftsmanship rather than machinery that gives hanji its special quality.

items.title: Water and Your Body
items.text: Doctors often advise people to drink more water, but few explain why. The human body is about sixty percent water, and every organ depends on it. Not only does water carry nutrients through the blood, but it also helps the body control its temperature. When people lose too much water through sweat, they may feel dizzy or find it hard to concentrate. Seldom does thirst appear until the body is already low on fluid, so waiting for it is not wise. Athletes in particular should sip water before, during, and after exercise. Still, drinking huge amounts at once is not helpful either. Steady, moderate drinking throughout the day is the best habit.

items.title: Honeybee Dances
items.text: Honeybees communicate in a remarkable way. When a worker bee finds a good source of nectar, she returns to the hive and performs a waggle dance. The direction of the dance shows where the flowers are in relation to the sun, and its length tells how far away they are. Rarely in nature do we see such a precise system for sharing directions. Watching closely, other bees learn the route and fly straight to the flowers. Had scientists not observed the dance carefully, this behavior might have remained a mystery. Today, researchers still study it to understand how small brains solve complex problems.

items.title: Volunteering at the Library
items.text: Last summer, I volunteered at my neighborhood library, and the experience changed my view of community work. At first, I expected to do nothing but put books back on the shelves. Little did I know that I would also help children learn to read. Every Tuesday, a group of six-year-olds gathered around me while I read aloud, and their excitement was contagious. Not only did I improve my own speaking skills, but I also made friends with other volunteers. It was the gratitude of the parents that surprised me most. They thanked me as if I had given them a gift. Now I believe that small acts of service can have a surprisingly large effect.

The thanks from the parents

items.title: The Night Train
items.text: I boarded the night train at ten o'clock, expecting a long and boring journey. Hardly had the train left the station when I noticed the stars outside my window, far brighter than any I had seen in the city. Across the aisle, an elderly man was knitting a scarf. We began to talk, and he told me he rode this train every month to visit his sister. Not until dawn did I realize how many hours we had spent chatting. Outside, mist covered the fields, and the first light turned them gold. By the time we arrived, my sense of boredom had vanished entirely. I had gained a new friend and a lovely memory.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: An unexpectedly pleasant overnight trip
